HTTP status codes are three-digit responses from a server indicating the result of a client's request. They are grouped into five classes: 1xx (Informational), 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client errors), and 5xx (Server errors). These codes help identify where communication breaks or succeeds. Sam mentioned encountering them in veltrix-core during debugging and troubleshooting after config mismatches. HTTP status codes are three-digit server responses indicating request results. They are grouped into five classes: 1xx (Informational), 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client errors), and 5xx (Server errors). HTTP status codes are three-digit responses indicating the result of a client's request. They are grouped into five classes: 1xx (Informational), 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client errors), and 5xx (Server errors). Common examples include 200 (OK), 201 (Created), 301 (Moved Permanently), 302 (Found), 404 (Not Found), 403 (Forbidden), and 500 (Internal Server Error). These codes help identify where communication breaks or succeeds. Status codes are often encountered in veltrix-core during debugging and after configuration mismatches. Understanding them aids in troubleshooting and clarifying errors during onboarding or API interactions.
